title: SSi exchange codex: the 6 exchange-grain conversational frames (X1-X6)
purpose: The definitions a model (Haiku family) uses to say which exchange frames an ADJACENT PAIR (or triple) of turns inside one scene instantiates. Tom 2026-10-07 (r-2026-10-07-never-use-regex-to-classify-language). A separate codex from D because the unit tagged is different: D tags one turn, X tags a rendered exchange 'A: ... || B: ...'. Mixing the grains in one codex would let a turn-grain frame fire on an exchange text and vice versa. The X-ids are pinned to tools/frame-layer/dialogue-patterns.cjs.
task: You tag short exchanges from a spoken-dialogue corpus (a language course's conversation pods, and clinical health-sector conversations) with exchange frames
request: Each numbered item is an exchange: two adjacent turns 'A: <first turn> || B: <second turn>', sometimes with a third turn '|| A: <third turn>'. For EACH numbered exchange, give the X-frame ids it instantiates, per the codex. Never output O: this codex has no openers.
example: Example: 3: A asks yes/no; B opens with yes + elaboration => X2
general_rules: An exchange frame is a relation BETWEEN turns: what B's turn does in reply to A's turn. Judge the relation, never the presence of a word in one turn.
A and B are adjacent turns in the same scene. Usually different people speak; if B's turn plainly continues A's own speech (same speaker going on), no exchange frame fires.
Only the turns shown count. Do not imagine a turn that is not there.
Multi-label: an exchange can instantiate several frames ('A: Do you have contactless? || B: Of course. There's the machine.' fires X2 and X5). Many exchanges fire none.
When unsure whether a borderline case fires, follow the frame's boundary rules; if they do not settle it, do not fire.
output: One line per exchange: '<number>: <tokens>' where tokens are X-frame ids, or '-' when there is nothing. Example: '12: X2 X5'.

frames.name: reciprocal return
frames.definition: A asks B a question; B ANSWERS it and RETURNS the same question to A (and you? / what about you? / and what do you do?). When a third turn is shown, X1 additionally requires that third turn to answer the returned question rather than ask something new.
positives: A: What's your name? || B: My name is Anna. And you?
A: Where are you from? || B: I'm from Manchester, but I live in London now. And you?
A: Where are you from? || B: I'm from Manchester. And you? || A: I'm from France.
A: How are you? || B: Fine, thanks. And yourself?
A: What do you do? || B: I'm a nurse. And what do you do?

near_misses.text: A: What's your name? || B: My name is Anna.
A: I'm a teacher. || B: And you like it?
near_misses.why: A asked nothing; B asks a new question

near_misses.text: A: Where are you from? || B: I'm from Leeds. And you? || A: What time is it?
near_misses.why: the third turn does not answer the return

near_misses.text: A: Shall we go? || B: You and me?
A: Are you tired? || B: Yes. How about a coffee?

boundary: B must both answer and return.
With a third turn shown, the third turn must answer the return.

frames.name: polar response to a question
frames.definition: A asks a question (normally a yes/no question, or an offer or request phrased as a question); B's turn OPENS with a polar answer (yes, no, yeah, of course, certainly, I'm afraid not), with or without an elaboration.
positives: A: Are you going to work? || B: Yes, I've got a busy day today.
A: Excuse me, is this seat taken? || B: No, it's free. Please, go ahead.
A: Would you like the menu? || B: Yes, please.
A: Did you have a long day? || B: Yes, very. I'm very tired now.
A: Could I pay by card? || B: Of course. There's the machine.

near_misses.text: A: Where are you from? || B: I'm from France.
A: I'm going home. || B: Yes, me too.
A: Is this seat taken? || B: No one's sitting there.
near_misses.why: 'no one' is a pronoun, not an answer particle

near_misses.text: A: Thank you so much. || B: No problem.
near_misses.why: a downgrade of thanks (X6), not a polar answer

near_misses.text: A: Can I help? || B: I'm looking for the station.

boundary: A's turn must contain a question that B's polar particle answers.

frames.name: repair
frames.definition: B signals that A's turn was NOT understood or not heard and asks for repetition, slowing down or clarification: sorry?, pardon?, I didn't catch that, I don't understand, what do you mean?, could you say that again (more slowly)?
positives: A: I'm a nurse, at the hospital just round the corner. And you? || B: I'm sorry, I didn't understand you. Could you say that again more slowly?
A: It's the third on the left past the lights. || B: Sorry, could you repeat that?
A: Take it twice daily with food. || B: Pardon?
A: We need a fasting sample. || B: What do you mean, fasting?
A: The 42 goes from stand C. || B: I didn't quite catch that.

near_misses.text: A: Is this seat taken? || B: Sorry, yes, it is.
near_misses.why: an apology, not a repair; A was understood

near_misses.text: A: Hello! || B: Hello! I'm sorry but I can't talk at the moment.
near_misses.why: an apology for not talking, not non-understanding

near_misses.text: A: Do you understand? || B: Yes, I understand.
A: My mother doesn't understand English. || B: I can help her.
A: Could you say that again? || B: Of course. I'm a nurse.
near_misses.why: B is the one REFORMULATING; the repair request is in A

boundary: The non-understanding must be B's, about A's immediately preceding turn.

frames.name: instruction -> read-back
frames.definition: A gives an instruction or information (not a question); B MARKS RECEIPT of it (got it, understood, noted, that's right) and/or SAYS IT BACK; or A asks B to say it back and B's confirmation of the read-back is marked ('word perfect', 'exactly right').
positives: A: Two tablets, twice a day, after food. || B: Got it. Two after breakfast and two after tea.
A: Bring the form back on Monday. || B: Understood, Monday.
A: Now say the three things back to me. || B: Rest, drink water, and call if the pain gets worse.
A: Rest, fluids, and call if it gets worse. || B: Word perfect.
A: Platform four, change at Cardiff. || B: Platform four, change at Cardiff. Thanks.

near_misses.text: A: Take two tablets. || B: Why two?
A: Do you want the receipt? || B: Got it, thanks.
near_misses.why: A asked a question, it was not an instruction

near_misses.text: A: Turn left at the lights. || B: I don't understand.
A: The bus leaves at six. || B: Lovely, thank you.
near_misses.why: uptake and thanks, no receipt marker or read-back

near_misses.text: A: I got the job! || B: Well done.

boundary: B's turn must explicitly mark receipt or repeat the content; plain thanks does not fire.

frames.name: order -> deictic handover
frames.definition: B HANDS OVER or POINTS OUT a physical thing in the situation (here you are, here's your coffee, there's the machine), in reply to what A ordered, requested or needs.
positives: A: Yes, please. || B: Here's your coffee.
A: Could I pay by card? Do you have contactless? || B: Of course. There's the machine.
A: Four single tickets to town, please. || B: Here you are.
A: Can I see the menu? || B: Here it is.
A: I'm ready to go home. || B: Here's your medication and your discharge sheet.

near_misses.text: A: What do you think? || B: Here's what I think.
A: Is there a bank? || B: There's one on the corner.
A: Where are we? || B: Here we are, the station.
A: Two coffees, please. || B: Of course. Anything else?
A: Do you have the keys? || B: No, I left them at home.

boundary: Fires only when B gives or points out an object to A in the situation.

frames.name: thanks -> downgrade
frames.shape: thank you -> not at all | no problem | you're welcome
frames.definition: A THANKS B; B DOWNGRADES the thanks: not at all, no problem, you're welcome, no trouble, any time, my pleasure, don't mention it, that's alright.
positives: A: Thank you so much. || B: Not at all.
A: Thanks for your help. || B: No problem, any time.
A: Thank you, love. || B: You're welcome.
A: That's very kind of you. || B: My pleasure.
A: Thanks for waiting. || B: That's alright, no trouble.

near_misses.text: A: Thank you very much. Goodbye. || B: Goodbye.
A: Can you help me? || B: No problem.
near_misses.why: A did not thank; B grants a request

near_misses.text: A: Thanks. || B: Thanks.
A: Thank you. || B: Here's your change.
A: Sorry I'm late. || B: Not at all.

boundary: A's turn must contain thanks; B's turn must contain a downgrade formula.
